name: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8
title: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 / WROOM-1U: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE 5 module, dual-core LX7, up to 16 MB flash and 16 MB PSRAM
summary: A surface-mount radio module built round the ESP32-S3 system-on-chip: two Xtensa LX7 cores at up to 240 MHz, 802.11b/g/n Wi-Fi at 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth 5 LE, with a 40 MHz crystal, quad-SPI flash and optional in-package PSRAM under a shield can. The WROOM-1 carries a PCB antenna (18 × 25.5 × 3.1 mm); the WROOM-1U has a coaxial socket for an external antenna instead (18 × 19.2 × 3.2 mm). Versions run from 4 MB flash without PSRAM to 16 MB flash with 16 MB octal PSRAM; the -N16R8 has 16 MB flash and 8 MB octal PSRAM and is rated -40 to 65 °C. It runs from one 3.0 to 3.6 V supply and brings out 36 GPIOs on 41 pads.
key_figures: ESP32-S3 series (ESP32-S3R8 in R8 versions), dual-core Xtensa LX7, up to 240 MHz
384 KB ROM, 512 KB SRAM, 16 KB RTC SRAM
16 MB quad SPI flash, 8 MB octal SPI PSRAM
3.0 ~ 3.6 V, supply able to deliver 0.5 A
7 µA typ (RTC memory on, RTC peripherals off)
36 (IO35-IO37 taken by the octal PSRAM on R8 versions)

notes: WROOM-1 has a PCB antenna; WROOM-1U has a socket for an external antenna. Within each type the versions differ in flash size, PSRAM size and type, and temperature range.
The flash clock is limited to 80 MHz by default and has no auto-suspend; a 120 MHz clock or auto-suspend is available from Espressif on request, as are the H4 and WROOM-1U-N16R16VA versions.
The PSRAM is inside the SoC package. Octal-PSRAM versions use ESP32-S3R8 or ESP32-S3R16V.
VDD_SPI is 1.8 V on the N16R16VA versions only.
With PSRAM ECC turned on, the R8 and R16V versions may run up to 85 °C ambient, with 1/16 of the PSRAM given up.
Ambient temperature is that of the air right around the module.

circuits.title: Typical application: supply, reset, boot, UART, JTAG, USB and 32 kHz crystal
circuits.description: The module on a base board with the usual parts round it. The 3.3 V rail reaches 3V3 with 22 µF and 0.1 µF to ground. EN has an RC start-up delay (R1 up to the rail, C2 down to ground, values open; 10 kΩ and 1 µF are the usual pair) and a reset push button, SW1 with 0.1 µF across it, which reaches EN through a 0 Ω link R7. A two-pin jumper grounds IO0 to select download boot. A four-pin UART header brings out VDD33, TXD0, RXD0 and ground; a four-pin JTAG header brings out TMS, TDI, TDO and TCK from IO42, IO41, IO40 and IO39. A two-pin USB OTG header meets IO19 (D-) and IO20 (D+) through 0 Ω links, each line with an unfitted capacitor place to ground. An unfitted 32.768 kHz crystal with 12 pF loads and a parallel resistor place can join IO15 and IO16 through 0 Ω links. The other GPIOs are free; the centre pad and both GND pads go to ground.

parts.note: EN pull-up of the RC delay; 10 kΩ is the usual value
EN capacitor of the RC delay; 1 µF is the usual value

notes: NC marks a position left empty by default.
Soldering the centre pad to base-board ground is optional and helps heat flow; too much paste there lifts the module and can spoil the joints on the edge pads.
The EN RC values are tuned to the supply's power-up behaviour and the chip's power-up and reset timing.
On the N16R16V versions IO47 and IO48 are in the 1.8 V domain.

operation.text: The module holds the ESP32-S3 SoC (ESP32-S3, ESP32-S3R2, ESP32-S3R8 or ESP32-S3R16V, the latter three with PSRAM in the package), a separate quad-SPI flash fed from VDD_SPI, a 40 MHz crystal, the RF matching network and either the PCB antenna (WROOM-1) or the antenna socket (WROOM-1U). The outside connections are the 3V3 supply, EN, the GPIOs and ground.

Inside, the 3.3 V rail is decoupled by 10 µF, 1 µF and 0.1 µF capacitors and protected by an ESD diode. The VDDA pins take 1 µF and 10 nF straight off the rail; the VDD3P3 pins are fed through a 2.0 nH (±0.1 nH) series inductor with 0.1 µF after it. The 40 MHz crystal is ±10 ppm with load capacitors chosen for the crystal and a series element (resistor or inductor, 24 nH to begin with) tuned to the board. U0TXD has a 499 Ω series resistor and the chip-enable line a 10 kΩ pull-up place left unfitted. On PSRAM versions VDD_SPI is fixed at 3.3 V or 1.8 V by eFuse and ignores GPIO45; on the others GPIO45 must not be pulled high at power-up.

Two 32-bit Xtensa LX7 cores with single-precision FPU run at up to 240 MHz, with 384 KB ROM, 512 KB SRAM and 16 KB SRAM in the RTC domain. The CPU can be shut down while the low-power co-processor watches peripherals for changes or thresholds.

Wi-Fi is 802.11b/g/n on channels 2412 to 2484 MHz, up to 150 Mbps on 802.11n, with A-MPDU and A-MSDU aggregation and 0.4 µs guard interval. Bluetooth is LE 5 with mesh, at 125 Kbps, 500 Kbps, 1 Mbps and 2 Mbps, with advertising extensions, multiple advertisement sets and channel selection algorithm #2. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth share the antenna through an internal coexistence scheme. RF figures are taken at the antenna port (a cable, and a 50 Ω external antenna on the WROOM-1U) including front-end loss, at 3.3 V (±5%) and 25 °C; channel range and transmit power are set in software.

Four pins are sampled into latches at power-up or hardware reset and hold their values until the chip powers down: GPIO0 and GPIO46 choose the boot mode, GPIO45 the VDD_SPI voltage, GPIO46 ROM message printing, and GPIO3 the JTAG source. After reset they are ordinary I/O. External pull resistors, or a host MCU, set a level other than the default. Each setting also depends on eFuse bits, all 0 when shipped; an eFuse burnt to 1 stays 1.

In SPI Boot the ROM loader runs the program from SPI flash. In Joint Download Boot a binary can be written to flash, or loaded into SRAM and run there, over UART0 or USB. The chip also has an SPI Download Boot mode.
During boot the ROM prints to UART0 and the USB Serial/JTAG controller by default; either output can be switched off by register and eFuse settings, leaving USB Serial/JTAG only or UART0 only.
GPIO3 picks the JTAG source early in boot together with three eFuses. It has no pull resistor of its own, so whatever drives it must hold a firm level.

EN is raised only once the supply rails have settled (tSTBL, 50 µs min after the supply reaches 2.8 V). Holding EN below VIL_nRST for at least 50 µs (tRST) resets the chip. An RC delay on EN, usually 10 kΩ and 1 µF, keeps the chip in reset until its supply is steady.

Three UARTs up to 5 Mbps with RS485 and IrDA, sharing 1024 × 8-bit FIFO RAM; two I2C controllers (100 kbit/s, 400 kbit/s, up to 800 kbit/s depending on pull-up strength, 7- and 10-bit addressing); two I2S interfaces (8 to 32 bit, BCK 10 kHz to 40 MHz, TDM and PDM); an LCD interface (8 to 16 bit RGB, I8080, MOTO6800, 40 MHz or lower) and a DVP camera interface (8 to 16 bit, up to 40 MHz); SPI0/SPI1 for flash and PSRAM (up to 120 MHz in 8-line SDR/DDR) and general SPI2 and SPI3 (master up to 80 MHz, slave up to 60 MHz; SPI2 has six chip selects, SPI3 three); a TWAI controller compatible with ISO 11898-1 (CAN 2.0), 1 Kbit/s to 1 Mbit/s with a 64-byte receive FIFO; full-speed USB 2.0 OTG with integrated transceiver; a USB Serial/JTAG controller (CDC-ACM plus JTAG, can reset the chip and enter download mode from the host); an SD/MMC host up to 80 MHz with 1-, 4- and 8-bit buses; LED PWM with up to 14-bit duty resolution; two MCPWM units each with three timers, three operators and a capture module; an RMT with four TX and four RX channels sharing 384 × 32-bit RAM; and four 16-bit pulse counters. Not every chip signal reaches a module pad.

Two 12-bit SAR ADCs measure 20 channels and can be run by the ULP co-processor in sleep to wake the CPU on a threshold. The temperature sensor spans -40 °C to 125 °C and reports the die temperature, which sits above ambient and moves with clock speed and I/O load. Fourteen GPIOs work as capacitive touch inputs; the touch sensor has not yet passed conducted-susceptibility testing.
At 80 MHz the SD/MMC clock phase can only be 0° or 180°, so board layout has to close the timing.

No antenna ships with the module. Certification used a first-generation monopole of 2.33 dBi gain. A replacement suits the 2.4 GHz band, is 50 Ω, has no more than 2.33 dBi peak gain and mates with the module's socket; another antenna type or gain may need further testing such as EMC.
The WROOM-1 has an antenna keepout zone beyond its top edge; the base board should disturb the antenna as little as possible. The WROOM-1U has no keepout zone.
Reflow once only. Keep the module away from ultrasonic welding or cleaning: the vibration can resonate the internal crystal and degrade or stop the module.
